fields.rank_math_description: Sale and transfer of shares in an Estonian OÜ: due diligence, share purchase agreement, notarial deal or e-Notary, and the Commercial Register update.
fields.content_blocks_0_content:
Changing the owner of an Estonian company is not as simple as setting it up. As a general rule, an agreement to transfer a share in an OÜ is concluded in notarial form, and the other shareholders have a pre-emptive right to buy the share before an outside buyer. A mistake in the form of the deal makes it void, and a mistake in the procedure opens the door to a dispute. There are, however, several routes. The deal can be signed at a notary in Estonia or remotely via e-Notary with an e-resident card. If the share capital is at least €10,000, fully paid and the articles allow it, the share can be transferred without a notary at all, through the register. And sometimes it is more convenient to change the shareholders through a capital reduction combined with a simultaneous increase.
We choose the route for your deal, check the company before the sale, prepare the agreement and documents, support the signing and update everything that changes afterwards: the shareholder register, beneficial owner data, the board and the bank.
fields.content_blocks_3_content:
Key facts

Topic Practical explanation
Form of the deal As a general rule, notarial: both the obligation and the transfer of the share
Remotely e-residents can sign the deal via e-Notary without travelling to Estonia
Without a notary If the capital is €10,000 or more, fully paid, and the articles, by unanimous shareholder decision, exclude the notarial form
Pre-emptive right Other shareholders can buy the share before a third party unless the articles provide otherwise
Alternative Capital reduction with a simultaneous increase: a change of shareholders without a notary when the capital is under €10,000
Pledge of a share Also requires notarial form as a general rule
Register The shareholders of an OÜ are shown in the Commercial Register
Beneficial owners UBO data is updated within 30 days of the change
Seller's tax Determined by the seller's country of tax residence; Estonia taxes the gain mainly on the sale of shares in companies rich in Estonian real estate
Company's tax The share transfer itself creates no tax at company level
fields.content_blocks_4_steps_title: How to transfer a share: 4 steps
fields.content_blocks_4_step_1: Send a request. The registry code, who sells and who buys, what portion of the shares, the price, whether the parties have e-Residency, and whether a pledge or instalments are needed.
fields.content_blocks_4_step_2: Get a roadmap. A notary in Estonia, e-Notary, transfer without a notary or a capital change: we pick the shortest lawful route and check the shareholders' pre-emptive right.
fields.content_blocks_4_step_3: Prepare and sign the deal. The agreement, consents, waivers of the pre-emptive right and documents for the notary; signing in person, remotely or by power of attorney.
fields.content_blocks_4_step_4: We update everything after the deal. The shareholders in the register, UBO data, the board, the contact person and the bank signatories.

fields.content_blocks_7_title_right: Key insight: it is not the notary that costs you, but what was not checked before the deal
fields.content_blocks_7_text_right:
Buyers of a share in an existing company often check only the price. Sellers check only the form of the agreement. Then it turns out:
  • The pre-emptive right. Unless the articles exclude it, other shareholders can buy the share on the same terms. A deal that bypasses this right is grounds for a dispute.
  • Unfiled reports and tax debts. The new owner gets the company with its whole history: register penalties, EMTA debts, unclosed periods.
  • Unpaid shares. If the capital contribution has not been made, the obligation to pay it may pass to the buyer.
  • The board and the bank. The share has been transferred, but the former owner remains a board member with access to the account.
  • The seller's tax. In Estonia the deal itself creates no company-level tax, but the seller pays capital gains tax in their country. For residents of Ukraine, there is also a CFC notification within 60 days.
Practical takeaway: before the deal, the articles, the register, the tax position and the bank are checked. We do this as part of the package, not after the problems have become the buyer's property.
fields.content_blocks_8_title_left: When a share transfer is not needed and when it is not enough
fields.content_blocks_8_text_left:
• You need to bring in an investor, not sell a share. A new shareholder can join through a capital increase: the money goes to the company, not to the seller.
  • Only the management changes. For that it is enough to change the board member.
  • You want to give options to employees. An option is a right to buy a share in the future; the tax consequences depend on the three-year rule. Read more on the page for start-ups.
  • The whole company is being sold. Besides the share, the board, access rights, accounting and obligations are handed over: this is a sale project, not a single deal.
  • You only need the company as an "empty shell". Sometimes it is cheaper to buy a ready-made company with a checked history or register a new one.
fields.content_blocks_9_text_right:
• Change of board member: often goes together with a sale
  • Share capital increase and issue: a new shareholder joins without a share sale
  • Share capital reduction: a shareholder exits with a payout from the company
  • Amendment of the articles: excluding the notarial form, pre-emptive right
  • UBO data update: within 30 days of the deal
  • Company liquidation: if the company cannot be sold
  • Ready-made companies in Estonia
A share deal is the beginning of changes, not the end. When the deal, the register, the board and the accounting are handled by one provider, the new owner gets a company with none of the previous owner's data left in it.
fields.content_blocks_10_content:
Four ways to change the owner of an OÜ

Method When possible Notary Timing
Notarial deal in Estonia Always Yes Notary appointment + 1–3 days for the register
e-Notary for e-residents The parties have e-Residency or an Estonian ID card Yes, remotely No travel to Estonia
Transfer via the e-Business Register Capital from €10,000, fully paid, the articles exclude the notarial form No Usually 1 business day
Capital reduction with a simultaneous increase Shareholders must change without a notary, capital under €10,000 No A few days, including the capital procedures
If the share is transferred under a power of attorney and the parties are abroad, the power of attorney is usually notarised and apostilled if necessary.

How to sell a share in an Estonian OÜ: in practice

Step-by-step process

  1. Review of the articles and the register. Form of the deal, pre-emptive right, transfer restrictions, whether the shares are paid up.
  2. Company check. Annual reports, tax position, contracts, the bank.
  3. Notice to shareholders. If the pre-emptive right applies, an offer to the shareholders or their written waiver.
  4. Agreement. Price, payment terms, seller's warranties, the moment the share passes.
  5. Signing. At a notary, via e-Notary or, if the conditions are met, via the e-Business Register.
  6. Register changes. The shareholders and, if needed, the board and the contact person.
  7. After the deal. UBO data within 30 days, the bank, e-MTA, the accounting.

Transfer without a notary: conditions

Condition What it means
Capital from €10,000 If lower, the capital is increased first
Capital fully paid Unpaid shares rule out the simplified transfer
Provision in the articles The articles exclude the notarial form for transfers and pledges
Unanimous decision Such a provision is adopted by all shareholders
Articles entered in the register A transfer is possible only after the new articles are registered
For companies with €0.01–€2,500 capital set up by e-residents, the way into this regime is a capital increase to €10,000 and an amendment of the articles. That is a few days of work, after which every subsequent transfer takes a day.

e-Notary

Estonian notaries conduct deals remotely: the parties join by video call and sign the documents with an e-resident card or an Estonian ID card. This is the standard route for owners abroad when a simplified transfer is not possible.

Taxes on the sale of a share

The share transfer itself creates no tax at company level. A seller who is an individual pays capital gains tax in their country of tax residence. Estonia taxes a non-resident's gain mainly when the company's value consists largely of Estonian real estate. An Estonian resident declares the gain and pays 22%. Read more in our article on taxes for companies in Estonia.

Obligations after the deal

The board must update the beneficial owner data within 30 days. Residents of Ukraine who acquired or lost a share file a CFC notification within 60 days; see the page for Ukrainian entrepreneurs. Banks and payment services must be notified of the change of owner, otherwise the account may be blocked at a routine review.
fields.content_blocks_11_faq_items_0_question: Do I need a notary to sell a share in an OÜ?
fields.content_blocks_11_faq_items_0_answer: As a general rule, yes. The exception is capital of €10,000 or more, fully paid, with a provision in the articles excluding the notarial form, adopted unanimously.
fields.content_blocks_11_faq_items_1_question: Can I sell a share without coming to Estonia?
fields.content_blocks_11_faq_items_1_answer: Yes. e-residents sign the deal via e-Notary by video call; without e-Residency, by a power of attorney notarised abroad.
fields.content_blocks_11_faq_items_2_question: What is the shareholders' pre-emptive right?
fields.content_blocks_11_faq_items_2_answer: The right of other shareholders to buy the share before an outside buyer on the same terms, unless the articles provide otherwise.
fields.content_blocks_11_faq_items_3_question: How long does a share transfer take?
fields.content_blocks_11_faq_items_3_answer: Via the e-Business Register, usually one business day. At a notary, the time to book and prepare, plus 1–3 days for the register changes.
fields.content_blocks_11_faq_items_4_answer: The notary fee depends on the value of the deal. Our services are at a fixed price after assessing the deal.
fields.content_blocks_11_faq_items_5_question: Does the company pay tax when the owner changes?
fields.content_blocks_11_faq_items_5_answer: No. Capital gains tax is paid by the seller in their country of tax residence.
fields.content_blocks_11_faq_items_6_question: Do beneficial owner data need updating?
fields.content_blocks_11_faq_items_6_answer: Yes, within 30 days of a change of owners or control.
fields.content_blocks_11_faq_items_7_question: What if the buyer wants to join the company with new money?
fields.content_blocks_11_faq_items_7_answer: Then a capital increase is more convenient: the money goes to the company rather than the seller.
fields.content_blocks_11_faq_items_8_question: Can a share be transferred without a notary if the capital is €2,500?
fields.content_blocks_11_faq_items_8_answer: Not directly. You can increase the capital to €10,000 and amend the articles, or use a capital reduction with a simultaneous increase.
fields.content_blocks_12_final_cta_title: Send us the deal parameters and we will find the shortest route
fields.content_blocks_12_final_cta_text: Give us the registry code, who sells and who buys, which share, and whether the parties have e-Residency. Within a business day we will tell you whether a notary is needed, which shareholder rights must be considered and what the turnkey deal will cost.
